Done. Summary of the incident repair:

## Fault discovered
`packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts` → `migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot()` (legacy `~/.pi/agent/*.jsonl` → `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/` migration). After computing the destination path it called a bare `renameSync(file, newPath)` (with the collision guard conspicuously missing, leaving two blank lines). On POSIX `rename(2)` silently replaces an existing destination, so a session already present at the destination lost its bytes and the legacy copy disappeared — both copies destroyed.

## Fix (3 lines, production code only)
```ts
// Never clobber a session that already lives at the destination: the
// existing file wins, so leave both copies untouched and keep going.
if (existsSync(newPath)) continue;
```
The `continue` keeps the loop going so unrelated legacy sessions still migrate.

## Regression — `.prale-eval/regression.mjs`
- Loads the **real** `packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts` through `.prale-eval/subject.mjs` (`loadModule`), faking only process boundaries (`chalk`, `CONFIG_DIR_NAME`, `getAgentDir`, `getBinDir`, `migrateKeybindingsConfig`, `stripBom`); `fs` is the real builtin so genuine rename/overwrite semantics apply.
- Seeds one colliding legacy session (alphabetically first), plus two unrelated legacy sessions (same cwd and another cwd), in a throwaway dir under `.prale-eval` (removed in `finally`).
- Asserts: destination bytes unchanged, colliding source still present with its own bytes, unrelated sessions moved with intact bytes, and a full file-tree snapshot equals exactly the expected set — catching overwrite, deletion, or duplicate/renamed copies.
- Verified: exit 0 on repaired code; with the guard temporarily removed it exits 1 with `ASSERTION FAILED: existing destination session was modified or overwritten by the migration` (fault copy then restored).

Only `packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts` is modified; `TASK.md`, `subject.mjs`, locks, and harness files untouched.
